name: SQL Formatter
description: Pretty-print, minify or validate SQL statements.

results.outputHint: The result can be copied directly.

examples.label: Format SQL
examples.value: select id, name from users where id = 1 order by name

examples.label: With a string literal
examples.value: select 'from where' as x from t

hints.input: The tool only tokenises and re-lays out whitespace; it never executes SQL and never changes the meaning of a statement.
hints.action: Validate only reports whether the statement can be tokenised; it does not rewrite the content.
hints.indent: The indent width is measured in spaces; 2, 4 and 8 are available.
hints.dialect: The dialect affects how keywords and functions are recognised; name it explicitly for cross-database statements.
hints.keywordCase: Only keywords are affected; identifiers and string literals stay untouched.
hints.output: Format breaks the main clauses onto separate lines; minify removes all redundant whitespace.

faq.a: No. The tool works on lexical units, so a literal such as `'from where'` keeps its content.

faq.q: Can it check whether a table exists?
faq.a: No. It never connects to a database and only tidies the statement locally.

faq.q: Do I still need to review the result?
faq.a: Yes. Dialect details still differ, and the tool only guarantees that the token sequence is unchanged.
